accepted_context: 3–4, 7: family names; Lucy distinction; only four Presbyterian members
actual_copy: Pearl of Great Price — Joseph Smith—History 1:3–4 and 7: Joseph names his father, Joseph Smith Sr., and his mother, Lucy Smith, formerly Mack, a daughter of Solomon Mack. The children named are Alvin, Hyrum, Joseph, Samuel Harrison, William, Don Carlos, Sophronia, Catherine and Lucy; Lucy the mother and Lucy the daughter are two people. Verse 7 reports Presbyterian membership for his mother, Hyrum, Samuel Harrison and Sophronia, not for the whole family. These are the narrator’s reported relationships, not corroborated civil records. See also: “Alvin in Joseph Smith's family account”, “Joseph Smith Sr.”, “Hyrum Smith”, “Samuel H. Smith”.
verdict: minimum prose conforms; canonical identity reuse remains separately open

accepted_context: 56–58: Stoal source spelling, failed mine, Hale parentage, Tarbill marriage
actual_copy: Pearl of Great Price — Joseph Smith—History 1:56–58: Joseph works for Josiah Stoal (the account’s spelling), who employs him in a search for a silver mine in Harmony; the reported search fails. Joseph boards with Isaac Hale, whose daughter is Emma. Joseph and Emma are reported married on January 18, 1827, at the house of Squire Tarbill in South Bainbridge; Tarbill is given no first name here. The failed mine search is kept as reported. See also: “Emma Smith”, “Joseph Smith—History: family moves, marriage and translation”.

accepted_context: 61–65: financial aid versus trip; relayed testimony, no independent certification
actual_copy: Pearl of Great Price — Joseph Smith—History 1:61–65: Martin Harris gives Joseph financial help with his move, and separately carries copied characters to New York City. Professor Charles Anthon and Dr. Mitchell (no first name given) appear in Harris’s account as Joseph relays it; the reported certification is not presented as an independently verified statement by either man. Joseph is not routed along Harris’s trip. See also: “Martin Harris”.

actual_copy: Pearl of Great Price — Joseph Smith—History 1:30–54 and 59–60: Moroni is the named heavenly messenger in the account. The plates, the Urim and Thummim, the breastplate, the stone box, the annual visits to the hill and the eventual return of the plates to the messenger are distinct reported objects and episodes; none is drawn as a separate pin. Receiving the plates on September 22, 1827 is not the first, 1823 hill visit, and the account’s “until this day” 1838 narration date is not the date of the return. See also: “Receiving the plates”, “Hill near Manchester (PGP)”.

accepted_context: 66–75: scribe, reciprocal baptism, directing authorities, future offices
actual_copy: Pearl of Great Price — Joseph Smith—History 1:66–75: Oliver Cowdery serves as Joseph’s scribe. Joseph baptizes Oliver and Oliver baptizes Joseph. In the account John the Baptist confers the Aaronic Priesthood on both; Peter, James and John are named as the authorities directing him, not as appearing in this baptism scene. Aaron, Levi and Melchizedek appear in priesthood terms, not as people present. Joseph’s promised office of first elder and Oliver’s of second elder are future offices, not a church already organized in May 1829. See also: “Reported baptisms”, “Susquehanna River baptism setting”, “Oliver Cowdery”.

actual_copy: Pearl of Great Price — Joseph Smith—History 1:11, 24, 36–41 and 69–72: James (the quoted epistle), Paul and King Agrippa (a comparison), Malachi, Isaiah, Joel and Elijah (quoted or anticipated prophecy), and Christ and divine titles are text references with the roles those verses give them.
